1.why: UI uses a clean sans-serif typeface with adequate letter and line spacing across cards and forms.

2.why: Instructions use sentence case without italics or all-caps, and text is broken into short blocks rather than dense paragraphs.

3.why: Layouts are single-column cards with large inputs and buttons that remain readable and well spaced at mobile width.

4.why: Most instructions are brief plain-language sentences such as “Create a test-only secret, then add it manually to your authenticator app.”

5.why: No explicit example format is shown for expected inputs like the authenticator secret or recovery-code pattern beyond pre-filled demo values.

6.why: User can proceed via short labels and single buttons without reading long passages of text.

7.why: Setup secret and recovery codes are rendered as plain text lists with no copy button or selectable convenience control.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent alternative is offered; the flow explicitly tells the user to add the secret manually.

9.why: Standard email and password fields are present so browser autofill can work, but no explicit password-manager or autocomplete attributes are evidenced.

10.why: Progress indicator and bold page titles plus prominent blue primary buttons make the current step and main action clear.

11.why: Each screen focuses on one primary task (sign in, confirm identity, create secret, save codes, etc.).

12.why: Green banners such as “MFA is enabled. Save these one-time codes now.” and “Recovery code accepted.” state outcomes and next expectations.

13.why: User can regenerate recovery codes, test a code, go Back, and retry actions without apparent lockout or penalty.

14.why: The observed error “We could not complete that request. Please try again.” is blame-free but does not explain the problem or how to fix it.

15.why: No timers, countdowns, or expiry warnings appear on reading or code-entry screens, allowing generous time.
